transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having a really hard time keeping things organized. Like, I’m trying to manage schoolwork and also my little accessories shop, and everything just ends up in piles—supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes. I look at it all and I don’t know what I’m supposed to do first.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yes, I do. Like in class, or if I’m watching a video for one of my business assignments, I’ll start off actually listening and trying to focus. But after a few minutes my mind drifts to charm designs or order ideas, and then I realize I missed a big chunk of what was said.
Did these focus and organization problems already happen when you were a child?

Yes, I think so. My mom still has notes from elementary school where teachers wrote that I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I was called on, and rushing through group activities. It wasn’t that I didn’t understand the work—I just had a hard time slowing down and waiting.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can feel restless or have trouble winding down sometimes, but I haven’t noticed a stretch where I barely needed sleep and felt unusually wired like that.
Do these attention and organization problems also happen in parts of your life outside of school and your shop?

I’m not really sure. I’ve mostly noticed it with school stuff and the shop, because that’s where I have to keep track of things. Outside of that, I guess I haven’t paid as much attention to whether it’s the same problem.
Do you have the same trouble staying organized with everyday things at home, like chores or keeping track of your personal belongings?

Yes, kind of. The biggest problem is with my schoolwork and my little accessories shop. Like, my supplies, receipts, due dates, and assignment notes all end up in different piles, and then I don’t know what to start with first. It’s not that I’m trying to be messy—I just can’t seem to keep it all organized at the same time.
Do you often feel like your mind is occupied by a lot of worry?
I’m not sure I’d say a lot of worry. I do get stressed when I’m behind or things are piling up, but I haven’t really noticed my mind being full of worry all the time.
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah, I think it got more noticeable after I changed schools. That was about two years ago—maybe a little over two years. I had to manage the business program and my accessories shop with less structure, and that’s when it started feeling like a real problem.
Do these problems ever make it hard for you to manage everyday responsibilities at home?

Yes. It’s made it hard to keep up with things I’m supposed to handle. I missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid is at risk. And with my shop projects, people I work with have started relying on me less because I don’t always keep things on track.
Before you changed schools, were these attention and organization problems already causing serious problems in your life?

Before I changed schools, it wasn’t really causing serious problems like this. It became a real issue after that change, about two years and a couple months ago, when I had to manage the business program and my accessories shop with a lot less structure.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I worry about things sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it excessive. It doesn’t feel like the main thing I’m dealing with.
Do you still often feel restless or fidgety, like it’s hard to stay seated or still when you’re supposed to?
Yes, pretty often. Even if I’m not actually needing to go anywhere, I feel like my body is kind of buzzing, like I need to move. It’s worse when I’m supposed to just sit still and listen.
Before you changed schools, did these focus and organization problems ever cause noticeable problems with your grades, work, or relationships?

Before I changed schools, not really in a major way. The noticeable problems have been more since then. Like now, I’ve missed required steps for my program, and my financial aid is at risk because of it. And with my shop projects, people have started relying on me less because I don’t always stay on top of what I’m supposed to do.
Right now, do these focus and organization problems also cause problems in your social life or close relationships?

Yeah, it does, at least with people I’m working closely with. Like on shop projects, people have started depending on me less because I don’t always keep up with what I’m supposed to do. And then with school stuff, I missed required steps for my program, so now my financial aid is at risk. That’s been really stressful.
Do you often interrupt other people or jump into what they’re doing before they’re finished?

Yeah, I do that. In class discussions or group critiques, I’ll jump in with my answer before the other person is actually done talking. Then I realize I kind of guessed where they were going, and I feel embarrassed afterward.
Do you also have trouble keeping track of things in your personal life, like appointments or errands?

Yeah. It’s mostly that I can’t keep my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. My supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—everything ends up in piles, and then I don’t know what I’m supposed to do first.
Besides school and your shop, do these problems also happen in another setting, like with friends, family, or daily life at home?

I’m not really sure. I notice it most with school and the shop because that’s where there are actual deadlines and people counting on me. At home or with friends, I don’t know if it shows up the same way, or I just haven’t paid as much attention to it.
At home, do you also have trouble getting everyday tasks organized?

Yeah, I think so. It’s like if I have school stuff and things for my little accessories shop, I can’t keep it all organized together. Supplies, due dates, receipts, notes for assignments—everything ends up in random piles, and then I just kind of stare at it and don’t know what I should do first.
At home, do you often forget or miss everyday responsibilities, like chores, errands, or appointments?

Yeah, kind of. It’s less like I completely forget everything, and more like if someone gives me a few steps to do, I’ll do the first part and think I’m done. Then later I find out I missed something important, like attaching a form or finishing the last part of an order note.
When you’re with friends, do you often blurt things out before thinking?

Yeah, I do that sometimes. Like in group critiques or class discussions, I’ll jump in with my answer before the other person is even finished. Then I realize I was just guessing what they were going to say, and I feel embarrassed.
